title: Directive studio — oddments & prototype directives
content:
Notes to self — quick, messy log from the directive studio (oddments).

Context:
- Purpose: explore compact directive templates that are robust to persona swaps and token budget constraints. Want stable output structure (bullets, JSON-like summaries) across model variants and under aggressive truncation/quantization.
- Quick constraints: keep seed directives <= 45 tokens, examples (where used) cumulative <= 180 tokens, prefer anchors that are natural language rather than schema code.

Hypotheses to test:
1) Short, role-focused directives + single short example stabilize output better than long multiexample sets when latency/budget is tight.
2) Swapping persona labels ("analyst" vs "coach") causes more layout drift than content drift — so bind layout explicitly in the directive.
3) Models trained on instructions prefer explicit counters (e.g., "Step 1:") for ordered lists, but unordered bullets are more robust when exemplar length varies.

Prototype directives (compact):
- D1 (summary-bullet): "You are a concise summarizer. Produce 3-5 bullets capturing core claims and one actionable suggestion. Use plain English"
- D2 (persona-anchored): "You are a pragmatic product coach. Output: (1) short diagnosis, (2) 2 mitigations, (3) one metric to track. Use <tag> around metric names"
- D3 (schema-hinted): "Respond with JSON-like keys: title, risk, steps. Keep values short (<= 20 words). No extra commentary"

3-example set (compact examples, for in-context seeding):
- EX-1: Input: 'user report: app crashes on checkout when coupon applied' -> Output: 'title: checkout crash; risk: high; steps: reproduce w/coupon, check stacktrace'
- EX-2: Input: 'user: docs are confusing; many questions about auth' -> Output: 'title: auth docs unclear; risk: medium; steps: add quickstart, example tokens'
- EX-3: Input: 'performance: search latency spikes at 95p' -> Output: 'title: search latency spikes; risk: high; steps: snapshot p95, profile queries'

Observed failure modes (recent runs):
- Template collapse: with D3 + EX set, model sometimes emits natural English paragraphs instead of JSON-like keys when exemplar length > ~200 tokens. Suspect context window heuristics favor freer-form generation if examples are too verbose.
- Persona bleed: swapping persona label from "coach" to "analyst" produced identical content but different ordering; ordering matters to downstream parser.
- Token budget brittleness: aggressive quantization on dedicated backend caused occasional token truncation mid-bullet, leading to malformed JSON-like outputs. Need stronger end-of-output guard (explicit trailing token like "<END>" or enforced closing bracket).
- Hallucinated metric names: when asked for one metric, the model invents proprietary-sounding metrics unless given example metrics. Add 1 exemplar metric per set to anchor vocabulary.

Repro steps (minimal):
1) Model: open-variant-A (v1.2) & quantized 4-bit; prompt = D3 + EXs + 'Input: <issue text>'
2) Set temperature=0.0 and top_p=0.85 (observed better diversity control than top_p=1.0 with temp 0)
3) Compare outputs: count successful JSON-like parses (regex for keys) over 50 samples.

Quick experiment logs (runs):
- Run 2026-03-02: D1 + no examples -> 68% outputs with explicit 3 bullets; notable that bullets sometimes used numbering.
- Run 2026-03-04: D2 + 1 exemplar metric -> hallucinated metrics dropped from 40% to 6%.
- Run 2026-03-07: D3 + 3 examples (verbose) -> JSON-like outputs 42% -> trimmed examples to short phrases increased to 78%.

Open questions / next actions:
- Try explicit closing tokens vs. trailing example with '<END>' to see if truncation errors reduce.
- Evaluate same directives with hosted-api vs dedicated quantized runtime to isolate quantization effect.
- Build a micro-benchmark: 3 directives x 2 exemplar lengths x 3 personas x 2 quant modes = 36 cells; target 50 samples per cell. Estimate token cost and runtime.
- If persona swaps still reorder outputs, add forced layout language in directive ("Always use sections in this exact order: title, risk, steps").

One-off prompt snippets (for quick copy):
- Compact diagnostic (one-line): "You are a product diagnostician. Given the user report, return a 2-line diagnosis and one 10-word mitigation"
- Guarded JSON (with closing token): "Return keys: title, risk, steps. End with <END> on its own line."

Random notes-to-self: use small seed sets when demoing to SRE; they care more about consistent keys than prose. When packaging for Console rollout, include both a single-example fallback and a canary that uses D1+D3 to compare structure fidelity.

End of oddments. This file is a messy workspace — prune and formalize into a lending template once a stable directive combination emerges.

-- Maya
